current_source_comparison.finding: Current development and stable 5.0.6/6.0.0 custom-variable parser and truncation methods agree. Stable full processors and upstream test files are byte-identical across the two release tags.

changes: Accept native numeric name/value components alongside strings.
Treat unmodeled root and tuple containers as information, never as proof of receiver rejection.
Retain positive-decimal slot spelling as heuristic warning, with PHP casts and configured slot limits external.
Warn on canonical array arity and unsupported native components because the pinned processor ignores that tuple.

Warn on strings over 200 Unicode scalar values after the exact PHP default trim-byte padding is removed, under the reviewed UTF-8 mbstring context. Numeric lexical width does not use the string warning.

oracle.method: Unchanged plugin processor and configuration helper executed in task-local official WordPress PHP-WASM. No complete Matomo application or HTTP server is executed.
seams: Common JSON reader uses associative json_decode with exceptions.
Common unsanitizer is identity; no HTML-entity inputs are used.
Request exposes the supplied decoded parameter map.
Empty base plugin/processor classes avoid unrelated application initialization.
Cache supplies explicit slot counts 2 or 8. Deployed configuration is not inferred.

limitations: This is decoded-parameter processing evidence. Query extraction, authentication, database persistence, full sanitizer, deployment state and alternate runtimes are not established by the stubbed oracle.
Full PHP native slot-key casting, architecture precision, alias collisions and deployment-specific slot count remain unmodeled. No slot maximum is guessed.

Root arrays and object tuples can retain data in the reviewed processor. Information findings identify unvalidated alternatives, not receiver errors. Components inside object tuples and root-array slots are not newly modeled.

The regex uses only PHP default trim bytes NUL, TAB, LF, VT, CR and SPACE. Form feed and nonbreaking space are not trimmed. The budget is fixed 200 in the reviewed helper, while configured slot count is separate. Unicode advice assumes the reviewed UTF-8 mbstring context.
Native numeric formatting and numeric overflow/coercion are not reproduced. A 300-digit JSON number is a boundary control against applying string width to numeric lexical text.
Empty strings are preserved for deletion. Malformed JSON remains an input-format finding, not proof of full HTTP request rejection.
These changes retain existing encoded-source duplicate extraction and complete-capture carrier behavior. No duplicate receiver-selection rule or new transport support is asserted.

The existing body extractor converts Unicode-whitespace-only strings to an empty scalar before format checks. Whitespace-only NBSP/form-feed strings can therefore exceed the PHP budget without a warning. Populated NBSP/form-feed controls preserve the precise PHP trim-byte boundary without claiming that gap is closed.
CustomVariables plugin availability, actual configured slots, complete bulk/plugin semantics and receiver versions outside reviewed implementations require external context.
